ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ is the altitude on side $BC$, and $AE$ bisects $\angle BAC$. If $\angle BAC : \angle B : \angle C = 4 : 3 : 2$, find the measure of $\angle DAE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In $\triangle ABC$,

since $\angle BAC : \angle B : \angle C = 4 : 3 : 2$,

thus $\angle BAC = 180^\circ \times \frac{4}{9} = 80^\circ$, $\angle B = 180^\circ \times \frac{3}{9} = 60^\circ$,

since $AD$ is the altitude to side $BC$,

thus $\angle ADB = 90^\circ$,

thus $\angle BAD = 90^\circ - \angle B = 30^\circ$,

since $AE$ bisects $\angle BAC$,

thus $\angle BAE = \frac{1}{2} \angle BAC = 40^\circ$,

thus $\angle DAE = \angle BAE - \angle BAD = \boxed{10^\circ}$.
